I am old now, 72 years, and my hands are not as strong as before. This small piece of land I have, I plant cassava mostly, sometimes sweet potato — they do not need much, and even when the rain is bad they give me something to eat. I have no money for the fertilizer from the shop, and anyway my neighbors here do not put it on cassava, only maybe on maize. I keep the few goats and chickens near the house, so I carry their droppings to the plot when I prepare the land — that is what my mother did and what I have always done.

For the cuttings, I take them from my own plot from last season, and sometimes my daughter brings me some from her plot. I do not buy seed. The cassava does not get sick much here, so I do not spray anything — I would not know where to buy such things, and I have no money for it. The rain is what waters my plot, I cannot carry water that far at my age. I do most of the work myself, slowly, but my daughter and her children come to help me when it is time to clear the land and when it is time to harvest. Sometimes I give a young man from the village a little something to help with the heavy digging.
